page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of x86_64 system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local NVMe storage or GPU accelerators, relying instead on network-attached storage options. Network connectivity is defined by a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the ecs.sn2ne.4xlarge delivers average multi-core performance, though its single-core capabilities are relatively weak. In stress-ng testing, the single-core CPU performance falls into the bottom 25%, and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression are rated as poor, falling into the bottom 10%. However, multi-threaded operations scale to average levels, as demonstrated by the multi-core stress-ng and bzip3 decompression results. Memory bandwidth remains consistently in the average tier, with read-only small block cached speeds at 655.24 GB/sec and uncached large block write speeds at 59.92 GB/sec.

The instance presents a clear tradeoff between single-threaded execution speed and multi-threaded throughput. While single-core tasks are limited by the older Intel Xeon architecture, the dedicated 16-core configuration provides stable, predictable performance for parallel workloads. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio offers a standard resource density suitable for workloads that do not require specialized hardware accelerators or high-speed local storage. This profile is appropriate for general-purpose workloads, including static web serving, Redis database operations, and moderate multi-threaded data processing.
